/-!
# Erdős Problem 215

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/215](https://www.erdosproblems.com/215)
- [Er83c] Erdős, Paul, *Combinatorial problems in geometry*. Math. Chronicle (1983), 35-54.
- [JaMa02] Jackson, Steve and Mauldin, R. Daniel, *Sets meeting isometric copies of the lattice
  $\mathbb{Z}^2$ in exactly one point*. Proc. Natl. Acad. Sci. USA (2002), 15883-15887.
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Erdos215

/--
Does there exist $S\subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ such that every set congruent to $S$ (that is, $S$
after some translation and rotation) contains exactly one point from $\mathbb{Z}^2$?

An old question of Steinhaus. Erdős was 'almost certain that such a set does not exist'.

In fact, such a set does exist, as proved by Jackson and Mauldin [JaMa02]. Their construction
depends on the axiom of choice.

The plane is identified with $\mathbb{C}$: the sets congruent to $S$ are the sets $uS + t$ with
$\lvert u\rvert = 1$ and $t \in \mathbb{C}$, and $\mathbb{Z}^2$ is the set of Gaussian integers.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 52, formal_proof using lean4 at
  "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/8822f7ddef30fadbd92e1c6ab4ed897af356af5e/src/latest/ErdosProblems/Erdos215.lean#L55"]
theorem erdos_215 : answer(True) ↔ ∃ S : Set ℂ, ∀ u t : ℂ, ‖u‖ = 1 →
    ∃! z : ℂ, z ∈ (fun w => u * w + t) '' S ∧ ∃ a b : ℤ, z = a + b * Complex.I := by
  sorry

end Erdos215

reformulations.difference: The plane is modelled as ℂ and ℤ² as the Gaussian integers {a + b·i}. "Every set congruent to S" becomes the images (fun w => u * w + t) '' S with ‖u‖ = 1, which are the orientation-preserving rigid motions only. The standard meaning of "congruent", and Jackson–Mauldin's Theorem 1.1 ("for every isometric copy L of the integer lattice Z² we have |S ∩ L| = 1"), range over all isometries, reflections included. Jackson–Mauldin also quantify over copies of the lattice rather than copies of S.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: (1) z ↦ (Re z, Im z) is an isometry ℂ ≅ ℝ². It carries the Gaussian integers onto ℤ², and it carries z ↦ u z + t (|u| = 1) to 'rotate by the matrix [[c,−s],[s,c]], then translate'. (2) Every isometry of ℂ has the form z ↦ u z + t or z ↦ u·conj(z) + t (Mazur–Ulam plus `linear_isometry_complex`). Conjugation maps the Gaussian integers onto themselves, so conj gives a bijection between f(S) ∩ ℤ[i] and (conj(u)·S + conj(t)) ∩ ℤ[i]. Allowing reflections therefore changes nothing; the source's own parenthetical restricts to translation and rotation anyway. (3) f(S) ∩ ℤ[i] = f(S ∩ f⁻¹(ℤ[i])), and f ↦ f⁻¹ is a bijection of the isometry group. So 'every copy of S contains exactly one lattice point' is equivalent to 'S meets every isometric copy of the lattice in exactly one point'. Proved in Lean in /workspace/review, all with axioms [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]: RHS ↔ ∃ S, ∀ f : ℂ ≃ᵢ ℂ, ∃! z, z ∈ f '' S ∧ z Gaussian (`erdos215_rhs_iff_all_isometries`); RHS ↔ ∃ S, ∀ f : ℂ ≃ᵢ ℂ, ∃! z, z ∈ S ∧ z ∈ f '' ℤ[i] (`erdos215_rhs_iff_jackson_mauldin`); RHS ↔ plby's ∃ S : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)), IsSteinhaus S (`fc_rhs_iff_plby`).

review.notes:
The file has a single declaration. Its theorem docstring copies erdosproblems.com/latex/215 word for word, and the [JaMa02] reference matches the site's bibliography. I confirmed the site's source tag [Er83c]. The site loads the full [Er83c] entry dynamically, so I could not check the module docstring's journal and page details for it; that is a docstring-level detail only.

formal_proof check: I downloaded plby/lean-proofs at commit 8822f7d (40 modules, ~15.7k lines, no sorry/axiom/native_decide/opaque). All 40 modules compiled against this repository's Lean v4.33.1 / Mathlib v4.33.1 in a scratch directory. `#print axioms Erdos215.erdos_215` (the theorem the link points to, L55) gives [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]. In a scratch file importing the compiled plby module, I derived the repository statement verbatim (`True ↔ ∃ S : Set ℂ, ∀ u t : ℂ, ‖u‖ = 1 → ∃! z, …`) from it, again with only those standard axioms. So `research solved` + `answer(True)` + `formal_proof using lean4` is correct.

Sanity checks: S = ∅ and S = ℂ both fail the ∃! condition, so the statement has no trivial witness. It is equivalent to the Jackson–Mauldin theorem.

The checkout already had a modified lakefile.toml and an untracked run/ directory, timestamped 12:21, before this review began. I did not create them; all my experiments are under /workspace/review.
